STUART A. WRIGHT

October 21, 2018–October 20, 2019

ii

STUART A. WRIGHT
Grand Master
2018–2019

A third-generation Freemason, Worshipful Brother Stuart Alexander
Wright was raised a Master Mason in Henry Know-Westlake Lodge No. 392
(now Wisdom Lodge No. 202) on October 22, 1986. He served as master of the
lodge in 1990 and in 1998 was presented with the Hiram Award.
Brother Wright has served the Grand Lodge of California in several capacities over the last 25 years. He served on the Insurance Committee from 19902014 and was the chairman for a total of 10 years. In 2011, he was appointed
to Masonic Homes of California Board of Trustees and elected vice president
in 2014. Brother Wright served as grand sword bearer from 2004 to 2005 for
Most Worshipful Brother David R. Doan. He has served on each of the constitutional boards.
In addition to his service to his lodge and our Grand Lodge, Brother
Wright has been very active in the concordant and appendant bodies. In
1988, he joined Al Malaikah Shriners in Los Angeles, where he served as
potentate in 2000. His service extended to the Imperial Shrine. He served
on the Imperial Athletic Committee; as director general of the Imperial
Shrine Convention, held in Anaheim, California in 2007; and as the chairman of the Board of Governors of the Shrine Hospital in Los Angeles for
three years.
Brother Wright is a 33° inspector general honorary in the Pasadena
Scottish Rite Bodies. He is a member of Signet Chapter No. 57, Royal Arch
Masons; Omega Council No. 11, Cryptic Masons; and Los Angeles Commandery
No. 9 Knights Templar. He also belongs to Dr. Rob Morris Chapter, Order of
the Eastern Star; St. Gabriel Conclave, Knights of the Red Cross of Constantine;
the National Sojourners; and the Heroes of ’76.
After a long career with the Insurance Company of North America, Brother
Wright is the owner and president of Stuart A. Wright Associates Insurance
Service. Brother Wright is an avid golfer and has enjoyed playing hockey for
a number of years, including five years with the L.A. Senior Kings. He and his
wife, Julie, live in Woodland Hills. They have five adult children and seven
grandchildren.

Grand Lodge F. & A . M. of California

5

ONE HUNDRED SEVENTIETH
ANNUAL COMMUNICATION

Friday Afternoon, October 18, 2019
The 170th Annual Communication of the Grand Lodge of Free and
Accepted Masons of the State of California was called to order by Grand
Master Stuart A. Wright on Friday, October 18, 2019.
Worshipful Brother Roland S. Castelar, Master of Wisdom Lodge No. 202
and Worshipful Brother Nathaniel R. Stiles, a Past Master of Wisdom Lodge
No. 202, raised the opening session of Grand Lodge. The gavel used to raise
Grand Lodge was presented to the Grand Master at a reception at Wisdom
Lodge No. 202. It is a five-sided gavel that represents the five lodges that consolidated to form Wisdom Lodge.
Reception of the Past Grand Masters
The Grand Master welcomed the Brethren and directed the Grand Marshal to
present the Past Grand Masters of the Grand Lodge of California at the Altar.
The Grand Marshal then introduced each Past Grand Master, and the Grand
Master and Deputy Grand Master personally greeted each one. The Grand
Master asked the Brethren to join him in saluting our Past Grand Masters by
the battery of three times three. The Past Grand Masters were then escorted
to seats reserved for them in the auditorium. The Grand Master then directed
the Grand Secretary to send to each absent Past Grand Master the usual letter
of greeting from the grand lodge.
Roll Call
The Grand Secretary was asked to call the roll of Grand Lodge Officers, Past
Grand Masters, and Past Grand Officers, and to ascertain if a constitutional
number were present to convene the Grand Lodge of California. The following were present as indicated by their response to the calling of the roll:

The Grand Secretary announced that, according to the Credentials Report,
there were 889 Master Masons registered as of 12 p.m. Friday, with at least 20
percent of the lodges chartered by this Grand Lodge represented, and that
therefore a quorum was present as required for the transaction of business.
The Grand Secretary reported that all lodges have paid their annual per
capita assessment to Grand Lodge.
Grand Lodge Opening
The Grand Master then opened Grand Lodge in ancient form. The Grand
Marshal and the Deacons retired to escort the flag of the United States of
America into the auditorium, which was followed by the Pledge of Allegiance.
Introductions
The following were asked to rise as groups for recognition:
Residents of the Masonic Homes and Acacia Creek, Diamond Jubilee
Award Recipients, Golden Veteran Award Recipients, Diamond Jubilee
Recipients, Hiram Award Recipients, Worshipful Masters, Lodge Secretaries
and Officers, Constitutional Board Members, Grand Lodge Committeemen,
and District Inspectors; each group was greeted with a round of applause.
The Grand Master also recognized Grand Lodge Officers visiting from
other jurisdictions.

Grand Master’s Message
The Grand Master then relinquished his chair to the Deputy Grand Master for
the purpose of delivering the Grand Master’s Message (Appendix A). After his
message, the Grand Master received a standing ovation and then resumed his
station.
Grand Treasurer’s Report
The Grand Master called on the Grand Treasurer, Very Worshipful Arthur L.
Salazar Jr., for his report (Appendix D).

The Grand Master called on the Grand Lecturer, Very Worshipful Ricky L.

Memorial Service
The Grand Master called on the Very Reverend David Y. Okamoto, Grand
Chaplain, to present a service of remembrance for our departed Brethren. His
remarks were as follows:
There are not words that come close to the ache we feel in our hearts when
a Brother of our beloved Fraternity passes—anguish, sorrow, grief, emptiness.

Grand Lodge F. & A . M. of California

15

No matter the length of time you may have known them, it’s difficult to show
how much we cared or miss them.
What is a eulogy? By Webster’s definition it is a commendatory oration or
writing, especially in honor of one deceased, but when it’s a Brother of your
lodge, or a Brother or mentor to you specifically, to me, it’s so much more.
Jim Rohn wrote, “If we are fortunate, we one day find that person who
impacts our world in such a way that our life is never the same again. By
chance, or by design, we met that someone who offers the support, encouragement, and inspiration to become more than we ever thought possible!”
For many of you, these are the people we remember with appreciation,
honor, and respect here today.
The Fraternity has lost 853 members of Grand Lodge this year alone. Just
think about that for a moment. Whether it be an Entered Apprentice, Fellow
Craft, or Master Mason, it was a loss to our gentle Craft. You may have not
known them well, but they made a difference! They made a decision to join
a lodge, a fraternity made up of many people from all walks of life, belief systems, and ethnic backgrounds, and in some way they made an indelible mark
upon someone or something.
Their dedication and self-sacrifice serve as a monument to the exemplary
men they were. Their humility, integrity, and hard work continues to inspire
those who knew them. My Brothers, we wish you good rest from your life’s
long labor, and as you look down upon us from the Celestial Lodge above
with our Great Creator, know that the world is most definitely a better place
because of you.
Steve Mason perhaps put it best, saying:
“From the depths of my heart, come the words of a Brother, where
our souls and our minds, are like that of no other.
We never lacked courage, or showed too much pride, with no
thoughts of guilt, or feelings put aside.
It’s important to strive forward, and not live through regret,
but to savor the memories, and to never forget.
To be such close companions, always made me so proud, never
scared to express my feelings, our emotions speak loud.
Whether it’s heaven or on earth, our souls are always together, we
share that sacred bond, knowing that Brothers last forever.”
This is how I will remember them, until we meet again my Brothers,
until we meet again…
At 11:38 a.m., the Grand Master called Grand Lodge from labor to refreshment, to be called on again on at 1:15 p.m.

Report and Video Presentation from
the Masonic Service Bureau
The Grand Master invited Worshipful Brothers Seb Badoyan and Mario
Balbiani to share a report and video on the Masonic Service Bureaus.
Worshipful Brother Badoyan shared his remarks, as follows:
On behalf of Worshipful Brother Balbiani and myself, we thank you for
this opportunity to tell you a little bit about the services provided to you by
the Masonic Service Bureau. First, a little bit of history.
The gold rush of 1848 brought many Masons to California, culminating in
the birth of the Grand Lodge of California in 1850. In 1855 four San Francisco
lodges joined together to form the first Masonic Service Board of Relief to aid
and relieve the heavy burden resulting from the great influx of Masons looking
for gold and the lingering effects of the typhoid fever and cholera epidemic.
In 1881, the Los Angeles Masonic Service Bureau was established and in 1950
the Greater Sacramento Area Masonic Service Bureau was established. In 1897,
our Grand Lodge established the Committee on Masonic Service Bureaus.
As you can see, the Masonic Service Bureaus have been “Your Partners In
Service” for almost 160 years. To learn more about the Masonic Service Bureau,
we invite you to view the following video and later stop by our booth in the
Exhibition Hall to pick up a flier that will allow you to use your Smart Phone
and iPads to also view this video, which we hope you will share with others.
At this point the video presentation was shared, and following which
Worshipful Brother Badoyan closed his remarks, saying:
Thank you my Brethren for your attention. Please don’t forget to stop by
our booth, take a flier and share the video with your lodge Brethren. We pray
that you will continue to support us and allow us to serve you as “your partners in service.”

2020 Junior Grand Warden Recommendee Randall Louis Brill
Brother Randall Louis Brill was raised a Master Mason in San Diego Lodge No.
35 on September 9, 2005. He served as master of the lodge in 2009.
Brother Brill has served the Grand Lodge of California in a number of
roles over the last decade. He was appointed grand chaplain in 2012. He served
on the Fraternal Support Services committee, Institute for Masonic Studies,
Masonic Education committee, and the Public Schools Advisory Council for
which he was the San Diego chairman. Brother Brill acted as a facilitator for
Grand Lodge leadership retreats and the Inspector Development Academy,
serving as the chairman of the program and of a recent task force to reorganize it. For six years, Brother Brill has served as a trustee for the California
Masonic Foundation and has been an integral leader in the Let’s Write the
Future Campaign.
In addition to this service, Brother Brill is active in the concordant and
appendant bodies. He is a 33° Inspector General Honorary in the Scottish Rite
Valley of San Diego. He served as venerable master of the Lodge of Perfection
in 2012 and has been general secretary of the Valley since 2009. He is a
member of San Diego Chapter No. 61 Royal Arch Masons, San Diego Council

20

Proceedings of the

No. 23 Cryptic Masons, and San Diego Commandery No. 25 Knights Templar.
He has been a member of the Al Bahr Shriners since 2008. Brother Brill is a
member of Inkopah Council No 86 Allied Masonic Degrees and served as sovereign master in 2012. He is a member of the San Diego Conclave Red Cross of
Constantine and Southern California Rosicrucian College.
Brother Brill received a Ph.D. in experimental psychology from Loyola
University in Chicago. After four years of teaching science and math at a private school in Illinois, he began a long career in marine mammal training and
research that led to research and leadership assignments around the globe. In
1975, he was a marine mammal trainer and training supervisor for the Chicago
Zoological Society. He went on to serve as a scientist and branch head of the
Scientific Veterinary Support Branch of the U.S. Marine Mammal Program, in the
Space and Naval Warfare Systems Command Center (SPAWAR) in Hawaii and
California. During this time, he received the Professional Achievement Award
from the International Marine Animals Trainers Association. He served as technical agent and contracting officer for the Defense Advanced Research Project
Agency. He was science advisor to the commander of the U.S. Naval Central
Command and Fifth Fleet in the Kingdom of Bahrain and received the Global
War on Terrorism Civilian Service Medal from the U.S. Department of Defense.
Randy finished his career back at the SPAWAR Systems Center in San Diego as a
leadership coach for the Lean Six Sigma Process Improvement program.
Randy and his wife, Susan, live in Escondido and they have four adult children.

Presentation of the Joe Jackson Award
This year, the Masonic Homes of California and our Grand Lodge were pleased
to present an award in memory of our late brother, Joe Jackson.
Joe Jackson, a Mason for 60 years and Hiram Award recipient, served
Joseph L. Shell Daylight Lodge No. 837 and Heartland Lodge No. 576 for 17
years as secretary, assistant secretary, treasurer, and chaplain. Joe exemplified
Masonic Relief and Brotherly Love.
The Grand Master explained that the Joe Jackson Lodge Outreach Award
is given to a lodge that has demonstrated excellence in outreach to their members and widows. The 2019 Joe Jackson Lodge Outreach Award was awarded
to El Segundo Lodge No. 421, for their extraordinary outreach efforts this year.
El Segundo Lodge creates a positive impact in difficult situations, while
maintaining a wonderful partnership with the Masonic Homes, Masonic
Outreach Services, and their sister lodge Beach Cities No. 753.
El Segundo Lodge maintains consistent communication and rapport with
their members and widows through their outreach committee. They are active
in the Lodge Outreach Program and host an annual fundraising event to support the Masonic Homes and Masonic Outreach Services.
Video Presentation
Most Worshipful Brother R. Stephen Doan reported on the progress of the
“Let’s Write the Future.” It is hoped that this theme will remind each Mason
to add a simple act of charity to our Masonic experience. Building upon our
commitment to help those most vulnerable among us in our Masonic Homes.
The Grand Master closed the evening out with an operatic performance
by Melissa Batallés.
The Grand Chaplain delivered the benediction and the evening drew to
a close.

Miss Julianna Barnes
Miss California Job’s Daughters
Most Worshipful Wright, Honored East and all attending Grand Lodge this
weekend, I cannot express how genuinely honored I am to be here with you
today, speaking on behalf of California Job’s Daughters. Today is actually
quite a monumental anniversary for Job’s Daughter’s. On this day, 99 years
ago, a woman named Ethel T. Wead Mick founded the organization of Job’s
Daughters, along with 180 young ladies in Omaha, Nebraska. She aspired to
create an organization for young women, where they could build professional
life and leadership skills while enjoying the influence and support of sisterhood. I find it quite fitting that today I get to commemorate this important
occasion with you, the men who give us our Masonic heritage—a connection
that is necessary in our organization.
Earlier this year I attended an event hosted by a Bethel that they called
“Ask a Mason.” The Bethel daughters requested local Masons to come and give
a presentation about Freemasonry. It was on this day that my entire perspective of Job’s Daughters and our Masonic family changed forever.
I remember sitting on the sidelines, listening to them explain the emblems
stationed in the Lodge room. They spoke of the pillars marking the entrance to
King Solomon’s temple and explained the representations of Heaven and Earth
that sit atop them. They explained why the Master sits as head in the East as well
as the significance of direction in the lodge room. Now, I was practically raised in
the lodge where my Bethel meets, but the next time I walked into our lodge room
was the first time I understood why black and white tile overlaid the blue carpet.
Not only did these Masons speak of the symbolic paraphernalia in the
lodge room, they explained to us the basic purpose and values of Freemasonry.
They emphasized that some of the objectives of Freemasonry were to promote patriotism, philanthropy, and tolerance in its members as well as in
people around the world.

Grand Lodge F. & A . M. of California

29

After the Masons had completed their presentation, a discussion was led
by the daughters. The girls asked even more questions about the history of
Masonry and the values it is based upon. Their curiosity led them to ask questions about not only the organization of Freemasonry, but the Masons themselves. The girls asked why these men had decided to join Masonry and what
they gained most from their experiences. They even asked to learn more about
the other Masonic organizations these men were apart of like the Shriners,
Royal Arch, and Eastern Star. Their excitement to learn turned into a passion
to support our Masonic family as a whole. These girls, including myself, were
so excited to be a part of this Masonic family that it made them even prouder
to be Job’s Daughters.
In Job’s Daughters, we talk frequently a the impact and importance of our
Masonic heritage. Listening to the presentation of these Masons led me to
realize that the “Masonic heritage” revered in Job’s Daughters is not simply
the recognition of our familial lineage, but, rather, that the lessons and values
of Freemasonry are reflected in the lessons we strive to teach and learn as
Daughters of Job.
With time, I came to realize the presentation given by these Masons
was a gift to myself and every other Job’s Daughter in that lodge room. By
simply sharing a bit about their order, these Masons were able to change my
entire perspective of an organization I had been an active member of for six
years. These Masons were able to give me an even greater appreciation of
our Masonic family as a whole, and for that, I will be forever grateful. I now
have this knowledge that I can share with other Job’s Daughters throughout
the state.
My advice to you would be to recognize that you can make an incredible
impact on our Masonic youth simply by getting involved and sharing your
appreciation of your organization.
I hope today that you don’t see simply a tall girl in a shiny crown, wearing
a long green cape, but rather a young woman that can be your guide and bridge
to an organization that is dependent upon your partnership.
By supporting our Masonic youth, you become a role model and I cannot
emphasize enough the power and importance of giving the youth of today an
example to look up to. You are capable of changing a young person’s life for
the better. You are capable of making that difference. It is because of you all,
that we are able to stand tall and grow strong together as a powerful, unified
Masonic family.
I would like to thank every Mason in this room who has taken time to
serve on their local Bethel’s Councils or helped in any way to pioneer Job’s
Daughters into our upcoming centennial anniversary. With your help and
guidance, we will be able to watch our young women grow into strong leaders
for the next hundred years.
Thank you, Most Worshipful Wright, for having me speak. Your wisdom
and love for the youth groups helps us all to grow stronger. Your welcome and

of California.

Mr. Brett Grimm, master councilor
Northern California Jurisdiction, DeMolay International
Most Worshipful Stuart A. Wright, Grand Lodge Line Officers, Grand Lodge
Officers, distinguished East, and guests here assembled: Hello and good morning! My name is Brett Grimm, and it is my honor to be serving as the Jurisdictional
Master Councilor of the Northern California DeMolay Association. At this time,
I would also like to introduce those who are here with me this morning. Please
rise as your name is called. Dad Terry Peters, Executive Officer of Northern
California and Hawaii; Dad David Killmer, Jurisdictional Advisor; Mom Jennifer
Jaeger, Jurisdictional Sweetheart Advisor; Miss Erin Foster, Jurisdictional
Sweetheart; Brother Aaron Pickett, Deputy Master Councilor; Brother Robby
Boyce, Senior Councilor; Brother Lennon Sanchez, Junior Councilor; and Miss
Cristina Morales, Jurisdictional Princess. Let’s give them a round of applause.
I’d like to start off this speech in the same manner I have every other
speech I’ve given to a Masonic body, by saying thank you for being the role
models I and every other member of DeMolay looks up to. As many of you
know, our founder Dad Frank Sherman Land was a devout Mason so it’s only
natural that we all look to you for guidance.
I joined DeMolay when I was 13 years old. I walked into the Masonic
temple on that warm May night wearing an old hand-me-down jacket that
was slightly too long in the sleeves and slightly too tight in the torso, but that
didn’t matter at the time. The only thing that mattered that night was that
I was joining an organization that I had heard my grandfather talk about in
high praise from time to time. As I walked into the building, I wasn’t sure how
I felt about this. It was all so foreign and different to me. We were invited to
sit down for dinner before the meeting, and after the dinner we were brought
to a room with two doors leading into a much larger room. My parents and
grandparents were then asked to go inside but I stayed outside and waited for
instruction. I then went through the initiatory degree where I learned about
the seven cardinal virtues, and following that I went through the DeMolay
degree where I watched a play about the heroic knight Jacques DeMolay and
his fidelity until death to his brethren. I watched the degrees and listened to
the lessons, but at first, I don’t think I took them to heart. I continued to go
to chapter meetings where I would sit through meetings and help plan events
and community service projects, but that was all I really did until one day

Grand Lodge F. & A . M. of California

31

something changed. My advisor, Dad Adam Wilson, pulled me aside during
dinner. He asked me about my plans for DeMolay and mentioned that I should
run for the line as Junior Councilor. At the time I agreed because I thought
it was expected that everyone did that, but later that night after the meeting
something happened.
I went home and I was preparing to go to bed but I just couldn’t fall asleep.
I kept on thinking about DeMolay and what I was doing. What would it mean
to be an officer of my chapter? What does it mean to show filial love, reverence for sacred things and beliefs, courtesy, comradeship, fidelity, cleanness,
patriotism, and the teachings of the heroic life and death of Jacques DeMolay?
This was the turning point when DeMolay began to shape me into the person
I am today.
After that night I decided that I wanted to make a change in DeMolay. The
next meeting, I turned in my letter of intent to run as Junior Councilor, and
continued to work until I finally was installed as chapter Master Councilor.
During your installation as Master Councilor you take another set of vows
that start off by asking if, “You promise to follow in the footsteps of Jacques
DeMolay should service and duty demand it?” This means something different
for every DeMolay, but to me it meant that I would continue to serve DeMolay
to the best of my ability, just as Jacques DeMolay did to the templars.
I continued to grow and learn more, but one of the greatest lessons I
learned was that in DeMolay, the difference is you. From the chapter member
learning his proficiency for the first time, to the International Master Councilor,
we all make a difference. We shape our organization based on our actions. It
doesn’t matter where you were raised, what your religious beliefs are, or even
what kind of suit you wear; what matters is that you wear the same DeMolay
emblem as your brother standing by your side. As DeMolay continues into its
next 100 years, it’s up to us to make sure that we are making a difference.
I still often find myself reflecting back on those thoughts that I had when
I first went in as Master Councilor. It’s easy to forget that we truly are the
difference in our order, and my hope for this organization is that every young
man will have this realization as well.
Before concluding, I would like to thank Most Worshipful Wright and the
Grand Lodge for the unceasing support you give to us. Some of the strongest
mentors I have in my life are Masons, and I owe that to DeMolay and our
Masonic support. I’d also like to invite you all to our annual convention happening from November 29th to December 1st at the Santa Clara Hyatt Regency.
Registration is live and available through our website at norcaldemolay.com
I hope that every member of DeMolay will someday realize that the difference is them so that we can continue to be the greatest youth fraternity in
the world. Thank you.

Miss Isabella Lynch, grand worthy advisor
International Order of Rainbow
Most Worshipful Grand Master, Officers of Grand Lodge, distinguished and honored guests, and friends of California Rainbow: Good morning! I am honored to
be here with you all today. I would like to start by thanking you for inviting me
to speak on behalf of the members of the International Order of the Rainbow for
Girls in California. I would now like to take a moment to introduce the Grand
Officers who are with me today. Would you girls please stand?
I want to share with you a memory that I have. A few years ago, I was at the
beach. I remember the warm sand between my toes, the sound of the waves
crashing over and over again. I saw a seagull soar off into the sky and in the
distance I saw small dark figures on the ground. I remember being confused
as to what these shapes could be. I started to wander off a little to investigate
and when I got closer, I saw that the beach was covered with thousands of
washed up starfish. They were so beautiful. The tide was barely reaching them,
and I quickly realized that these starfish were going to die if they weren’t in
the water. I immediately began picking up and throwing as many starfish as I
could. There was nothing stopping me then, someone tapped me on the shoulder. It was an older man and he told me that what I was doing was pointless
because I couldn’t possibly save them all. I looked at him and I was puzzled. I
couldn’t believe someone told me I shouldn’t try to help them.
I looked towards the sea, the sun was setting, and I felt overwhelmingly
hopeful. I picked up another starfish and threw it as far as I possibly could and
with tears in my eyes, I told him that I made a difference to that one. I’m sure
many of you have recognized this story. For those of you who don’t, it was
originally written by Loren Eisley.
One of the key ideas that Most Worshipful Grand Master Wright has
focused on this year is the importance of an individual and the role they can
play within the Masonic family. One person can determine the level of happiness they achieve, the words they choose, how they measure their fulfilment in
life, and what their experience in the Masonic family is like. Most importantly,
one person can leave their mark on the world in greater ways than anticipated
if they only make the choice.
In our organization, there is a saying: you get out of Rainbow what you
put into it. Although we use this expression in our order, it is not exclusive
to Rainbow. This idea is true in each and every one of our lives. Every morning we wake up and are presented with a choice: to get out of bed—maybe
after hitting the snooze button a few times! We go about our responsibilities and fulfil our day-to-day tasks and for most of us, we go to our Masonic
orders. Whether our day is productive, impactful, and worthy is entirely up
to us. We decide how we invest our time and what our attitude towards the
day will be. We determine our thoughts and our choice of words. Simply
waking up with breath in our lungs is a blessing and an opportunity to make
a difference, big or small.

Grand Lodge F. & A . M. of California

33

When deciding on what to share with you today, I thought about the starfish story. How a hopeful little girl tried to make a difference and was told
that her contribution was so minor that it wouldn’t matter. I love the attitude
that she has. Even though this world is too big to touch every single life, every
single life that we do touch still makes a difference. Instead of focusing on the
negatives, I encourage us to take a step back and change our perspective. In
our Masonic family, our investments may not impact every person on Earth
but with every act of service we perform, a life can be changed. What if the
gentleman had joined her? Instead of saying what are you doing, you can’t
possibly save them all, they could have made a greater impact together. I find
it interesting that he never asked her why she was doing what she was doing.
Sometimes in our orders we only question what the organizations are
doing but not why they are doing it. The reasoning behind a decision makes
a big difference. As a lot of you know, this year California Rainbow is working hard to raise money for The Painted Turtle, our statewide Grand Service
Project. The Painted Turtle is a camp for children who have chronic medical
conditions such as cerebral palsy, hemophilia, spina bifida, and so many more.
I picked The Painted Turtle because when I was nine years old, I was diagnosed with Juvenile Fibromyalgia which is a chronic pain condition. I have
been told my whole life that I don’t look sick, that my pain is an illusion, that
I’m just being dramatic. At first this hurt me, but as time went by it kind of
made me laugh. I was actually being bullied for something that I can’t control,
and their only reasoning was that they couldn’t see it. Yes, you cannot see
my nerves, but I assure you I can still feel them. You can’t see a headache but
that does not mean it doesn’t exist. I never let Fibromyalgia hold me back.
I was in sports, theater, ASB, Rainbow. In the same way, these children are
constantly making a bigger effort than healthy kids, andhey deserve a chance
to have fun and make new friends without having to worry what other people
think—and it’s absolutely free. The point is, if we can help just one kid go
to this amazing camp that would be wonderful, but if we can help two, that
would be extraordinary.
Every one of us has so much potential to make an impact on others. The
beautiful part about our orders is that we are all built on the foundation of
service. From Masonry to Job’s Daughters to Eastern Star to DeMolay, we all
have a spirit of service embedded in each of our hearts. By combining our individual efforts, we can see that small differences transform into a vast network
of service. For instance, like the starfish, if every single person in our Masonic
family brought in one new member, then our numbers would double. In our
organizations and in our day to day lives, we should make a conscious decision
to find our why and the why of others. This way we can understand how we
should show our love and support to the members of our Masonic families.
Just remember to never underestimate the power of an individual, especially
when that individual is a part of an amazing Masonic order. I want to personally
invite you to California Grand Assembly in Fresno for our 98th Convention,

34

the Enchanted Forest—Dream, Lead, Believe from April 4th through the 7th.
Thank you for listening to my interpretation of the starfish story and I hope
that each of us choose to make a difference in someone else’s life.
Mr. Eddie Mendoza, master councilor
Southern California, DeMolay International
Good Morning, Most Worshipful Stuart A. Wright, Right Worshipful John E.
Trauner, California Masons, friends and family; thank you for the invitation
to attend Grand Lodge on behalf of Southern California DeMolay. Your continued support is greatly appreciated. I had the pleasure of traveling to the
beautiful city of San Francisco along with our team of Jurisdiction Officers,
Brother Andrew Caster, Southern California Jurisdiction Congress Secretary,
Miss Megan FitzGerald, our Jurisdiction Sweetheart, and last but certainly not
least Miss Sami Maples, our Jurisdiction Princess.
Our theme for this year is Mission: Possible. Much like the fictional world
would not function without its covert intelligence agencies, the Masonic families rely on each other to grow and prosper. The mission for our agents this
weekend is to serve as your liaisons to the world of DeMolay. We are continuously seeking to learn more about the world around us, including the Masonic
families. As we continue to learn, we are not only gaining knowledge, but
also the experience you as our mentors pass down to us. A fantastic year has
passed under the leadership of Most Worshipful Wright and I hope the growth
continues under the leadership of Right Worshipful Trauner. You chose your
path to become a better version of yourself; when the opportunity comes, I
hope you will decide to pass your knowledge onto another.
Robert Ingersoll stated that, “We rise by lifting others.” That is the pay
you receive from helping another reach the goals they set in their Masonic
story. My father’s Masonic journey began in his teens. He took up a job at an
accounting firm where he later discovered that his boss, Mr. Davidoo, was a
Mason and a Shriner. My father’s boss sponsored from youth all over the world
to travel to the United States and receive treatment for conditions such as
scoliosis at the Shriners Hospital for Children totally free of charge. As a result
of his work over the years, my father was exposed to the world of Masonry.
However, when he approached his boss about joining, he was advised to postpone his admission as my parents had just decided to start a family and that’s
where his focus should remain.
After some time, my father left the firm and pursued his career while
learning about being a father and husband. Mr. Davidoo had left a lasting
impression and over time my father made his way back to him; never forgetting the lessons he had witnessed as a result of his early exposure to Masonry
and exemplified by the man he so earnestly respected.
My father took the time away to assess himself and his relationships and
when he felt he had properly prepared, he petitioned the lodge where Mr.

Grand Lodge F. & A . M. of California

35

Davidoo had his membership. Shortly after he became a Mason, I became a
DeMolay; and together we have gathered knowledge on the lessons taught and
how applying them daily can change the way we live for the better.
Just like the “Impossible Mission Force” team prepares for a mission,
and my father prepared to become a Mason, Freemasonry prepares you for
yet another step in your life:the role of a mentor. DeMolay would not survive
without mentors to guide our growth with a careful hand. We would like you
to assess where you are in life and determine whether you are confident in
who you are and what you stand for in order to be ready to pass on what you
know onto another. The time-honored mission of an agent has been to get in
and get out without anyone knowing you were ever there and I extend to you
the same challenge. The job of a mentor is not the most glorious and may not
win you awards or flowers; however, the reward you will receive will be the
knowledge that you made a difference in someone’s life and the satisfaction
of a job well done. Though the skills we receive are greatly appreciated, no spy
is complete without a few cool gadgets and gizmos, if you want to pass those
down to us too, we wouldn’t be opposed to it. A word to the wise though: I’d
suggest you keep anything flammable away from us, we DeMolay don’t have a
good history with fire.
This past September our DeMolay accepted their mission to explore,
gather intelligence, and bring tools back for DeMolay. These tools will carry
into their daily lives and prepare them for future missions.
The DeMolay of SCJ have accepted their mission. You have an opportunity: your mission, should you accept it; to infiltrate your local chapter and
support their activities, attend their meetings, and be that agent who leaves
a lasting impression and makes a difference in a young man’s life. Working
together, this is Mission: Possible!

GRAND MASTER’S MESSAGE
Most Worshipful Past Grand Masters, fellow Grand Lodge Officers,
Inspectors, Masters, Wardens, distinguished guests and all brethren in attendance, welcome to the 170th Annual Communication of the Grand Lodge of
Free & Accepted Masons of California and thank you so much for attending.
It is my obligation under the California Masonic Code and my privilege
to speak to you about my official acts during the year, the general condition
of Masonry in this jurisdiction, and my recommendations for legislation. A
written copy will be in the proceedings.
It was a year ago when I stood before you and spoke of my theme
“Freemasonry—the Difference is You.” I expressed some very simple goals for
the year:
1) to increase excitement in the craft;
2) to increase enthusiasm in the craft;
3) to increase commitment of members; and
4) to ensure that fun existed. Through my visits to lodges, concordant
bodies, ballparks, and meet and greets, I have endeavored to promote those
four goals in my talks and by my actions. Proudly, I have noticed improvement
up and down our state in all four of these areas—something that has been
confirmed by others.
Many anniversaries took place during this term. It was a great honor for Julie
and I, along with the Grand Marshal and others to celebrate the 75-year Diamond
Jubilee Award presentation to five Brothers—two of whom are sadly no longer
with us. The presentations were held at either the home or the lodge of each
Brother. The Brothers were grateful for those in attendance. The lodges, in each
instance, made the event memorable and they were the highlight of the year!
I presented 50-year Golden Veteran’s Awards to Most Worshipful John
Heisner, Past Potentate Dennis Shaffer, our Grand Marshal and Past Potentate
Ken Judd. For one of the awards, I made a surprise visit, which neither the recipient nor their lodge knew about. It was an exciting evening to say the least.
I also presented Hiram Award certificates to the Master of the Lodge for
presentation to Most Worshipful Mel Stein, Right Worshipful Emil Joseph,
and Worshipful Hampo Nazarian of my own lodge.

44

Proceedings of the

In San Diego we hosted the 40th Anniversary of the Conference of the Three
Californias. The conference brings together the Grand Lodge of California, the
Grand Lodge of Baja California, and the Grand Lodge of Baja California Sur in
Mexico. We also invited the Prince Hall Grand Lodge of California, represented
by their Grand Master, Most Worshipful Sam King; as well as the Grand Lodge
of Iran in exile, represented by their Grand Secretary, Right Worshipful Farhad
Yousefi. This exchange of ideas and exposure to degrees in Mexico over the last
four decades has broadened our knowledge of the differences and similarities
between our grand lodges. Each year we note the spirit of our southern brothers
and the fact that they are so strong and serious about the Craft.
The 50th Anniversary of the California Masonic Foundation was celebrated
at the fabulous Biltmore Millennium Hotel in Los Angeles with a huge gala entitled “Vivat.” The evening included prominent speakers and the audience was
packed. This was the largest festive board ever and some slurring during the
evening certainly occurred—there were seven toasts, after all. This year the
California Masonic Foundation continued the Let’s Write the Future campaign.
Many individuals and lodges dug deep to make historic donations. You will hear
more about this when the foundation gives its report tomorrow. My congratulations to all those who worked diligently to make this campaign so successful.
I also wanted to highlight a specific anniversary this year. Your Grand
Lodge was involved in the 100th Anniversary of DeMolay International two
years in advance. I set up a teleconference network with the northern and
southern California DeMolay jurisdictions and appointed Right Worshipful
Brother Glenn Woody chair of the group. Through regular phone calls and
follow up, the group explored ways that our Grand Lodge could participate
in this special centenary celebration. Many ideas were proposed and eventually adopted, including a special DeMolay issue of the California Freemason
magazine, symposia on the history and ritual of DeMolay in the north and
south, and an Honorary DeMolay Degree to be held tonight on this stage.
The north celebrated with a special degree class at Union City and a dedication of a bench and time capsule. The south celebrated with a dedication
of a bench and time capsule at Covina and the naming of “DeMolay Drive”
on the campus. The final event was the actual Centenary Celebration, hosted
where it all started with Dad Land in 1919 and where DeMolay International is
still headquartered: Kansas City, Missouri. There was a celebration and bricks
were purchased for a walkway to be installed by the statue of Dad Land. Your
Grand Lodge purchased a brick, as did our Grand Secretary with a personal
donation. I participated in the Kansas City celebrations with Julie and interacted with the kids and adults from northern and southern California. We
were honored to be with them as they are all so special to us. It was fun being
torn for attention between the north and the south and some very strong
bonding took place. I would like to personally acknowledge and thank Right
Worshipful Glenn Woody for his true leadership, patience and perseverance
in getting us to the point we needed to be. If you want to do something to

Grand Lodge F. & A . M. of California

45

help this great organization and make a difference, get involved as an adult
leader or get your lodge to set up a new chapter. It only takes five people, three
Master Masons and two others. Take a stand—do your part! Believe me, you
will be re-energized by these terrific boys and girls.
We attended three Masonic conferences this year and respectfully declined
one. The World Conference of Regular Masonic Grand Lodges was held in
Panama and the French National Grand Lodge Annual Communication was
held in Paris. The Conference of Grand Masters and the Western Conference
was held in South Dakota in February; I repeat—in February! We reluctantly
declined to attend the Annual Communication of the Grand Lodge of the
Philippines due to the hostile situation close to where the event was to be held
and the US State Department advisory not to travel to this location. We would
have had 15-20 people traveling with us and I did not want the responsibility
for their safety if something unfortunate were to happen.
It was a pleasure to appoint and install our new Assistant Grand Organist
Jonathan Davis early in the grand lodge year. We are so fortunate as he plays
both the organ and the piano. I was also honored to be asked to open grand
lodge and dedicate the organ loft at Oakland Durant Rockridge Lodge No. 188
in memory of Worshipful Brother Christopher Putnam, our late Assistant
Grand Organist, whom we dearly miss.
It was a joy and honor to open grand lodge at Destiny Lodge No. 856 in Covina
preceding the cornerstone ceremony for the new health center at the Masonic
Home on July 13, 2019. This skilled nursing center, which includes memory care
for dementia and Alzheimer patients, will be a critical addition to the Covina
campus—and long awaited. We all can be proud of the Masonic Homes for all they
do. The services provided are superior to others, and if you have not yet visited
either campus, I encourage you to put it on your list of “to dos” for 2020.
Over the past four years, I have had the opportunity to observe the growth
and impact of our Masonic Center for Youth and Families (MCYAF) program in
California. It remains a hidden gem amongst the many valuable and needed services offered by our great Fraternity. In order to address its future, I will recommend to our next Grand Master that he initiate a study of the structure of MCYAF
and look for the best model to support and continue the growth and expansion of
this service, which is greatly needed within our Fraternity and in our communities.
At my urging, the Pasadena Scottish Rite Bodies hosted a Mason of the
Year event for the first time in 2019 for lodges in Division VII. It was a big
success! Members were actually turned away at the door because the facility
reached capacity. I had the privilege to present each honoree with his award
after a great dinner. I thank the Scottish Rite for taking on this new project
and I’m happy to report that it will be continued in the future.
Recognizing that many of our brothers and their families in outlying areas
do not get a chance to meet or mingle with Grand Lodge Officers and particularly the Grand Master, I decided to set up four events in these areas as
a “meet and greet” gathering. I asked Worshipful Brother Vernon Dandridge

46

Proceedings of the

to organize these through our AGLs. After getting past the “You want me
to do what?” we sat down and set up a few rules: they would take place in
low-populated areas and feature light food and drinks, good conversation,
and absolutely no speeches. They turned out to be very successful and we
learned that those who attended appreciated the fact that Grand Lodge cared
enough to meet them in their own surroundings. These were held at Redlands
in November, Antelope Valley in February, Truckee in July, and Oakhurst in
September. Thank you, Worshipful Brother Vern, for your help.
Regarding our AGLs, Worshipful Brother Matt Ross of Division V retired
mid-year for personal reasons and was replaced by Worshipful Brother Bob
Beeson III. In Division IX, Worshipful Brother Tom Colgan decided to retire
at the close of this Annual Communication, after many years of dedicated service. We shall truly miss him and offer him Godspeed in his future. He will be
replaced by Worshipful Brother John Crago III.
In thinking about our future and where your Grand Lodge may want to
be, I established what I termed the “Elected 4” meetings. The Elected 4 are
the Grand Master, Deputy Grand Master, and the Senior and Junior Grand
Wardens. We met away from our residences and Grand Lodge and strictly
focused on one specific area of concern: the future. The goal of our discussions, brainstorming, and planning was to establish a 2050 Vision. What might
we want to look like in 2050, and what needs to be done now to reach that
goal? The Deputy Grand Master has agreed to continue this committee and a
report will be made at the next Annual Communication.
The Elected 4 put in place a steering committee on leadership development. The steering committee is a group of talented personnel with skilled
leadership qualities. Five sub-committees are under this steering committee,
each with its own chairman reporting to the steering committee, which in
turn reports to the Executive Committee. The sub-committees include membership development, lodge leadership development, inspector development,
AGL development, and board and committee development. While the names
look familiar, within each sub-committee new ideas are being developed and
adopted. These iseas will become standard for years to come and each will
have a relevance to the 2025 plan and even 2050. Your Executive Committee
is looking forward to big things from this special committee.
The 2025 planning effort was kicked off with a meeting of the board leadership in July, which brought together the chair, vice chair, president, and vice
president of our five separately incorporated entities: Acacia Creek, California
Masonic Foundation, California Masonic Memorial Temple, Masonic Homes
of California, and Nob Hill Masonic Center. This type of meeting had not been
held for some time but the plan is to now hold it twice a year. Each entity will
participate in the 2025 plan and while each may have their own goals, all will
be tied into the Fraternity’s 2025 plan.
Standing out from other U.S. grand lodges, we’ve established 23 new
lodges since 2016. This strategy is working well. None of the new lodges own

Grand Lodge F. & A . M. of California

47

buildings and they meet in various types of locations. The powers we invest
upon the new lodges allow them to focus on the practice of Masonry and
relieves them of the burdens of financial, administrative, and real estate challenges. The enthusiasm and excitement of these particular lodges needs to
seep into many other lodges, which would be rejuvenated by it. A number of
additional new lodges are being considered and we are identifying areas where
Masonry needs greater presence and recognition.
Some 25 years ago, meetings with the Prince Hall Grand Lodge of
California led to our mutual recognition and agreement of concurrent jurisdiction in California. I am pleased to say that our mutual relationship is strong
and getting stronger. We held new meetings with our Prince Hall Brothers this
year and reached an agreement to form a committee of both grand lodges to
explore how we can work even closer together and share common interests.
We look forward to the results of this committee in the near future.
Many grand lodge buildings around the world have within their walls one
or more lodge rooms. Though our first two grand lodge buildings had several
lodge rooms, this memorial temple has not had a single lodge room until now.
On September 20, I opened Grand Lodge in our new Freemasons’ Hall, and
we dedicated it in Ancient Form. We currently have nine lodges meeting there.
Lodges from around the state are inquiring about holding special meetings
there and visitors from around the world are touring it each week. If you have
not seen Freemasons’ Hall, be sure to take time to visit it as it is completely
unique and something you can be really proud of.
Each year I have attended the Annual Communication the Grand Master’s
message is positive and loaded with good stuff until this section comes up:
suspended lodges. The sad part of being Grand Master, even though it is part
of the responsibility, is dealing with the non-compliance of our Code. It pains
me that although we all knelt at the altar some, for whatever reason, feel
they need to violate their promises with senseless acts that have unfortunate
impacts on their lodge. If we are to be true Brothers and profess to have real
friendships, we need to act the part. We need to know and follow the rules
we’ve all agreed to and respect one another. Criticism of others is not healthy,
but praise is golden. Look for the best in others and stop the pettiness. Stop
the Facebook issues. Let’s be Masons. The following lodges were suspended
during my term: Artesia Sunrise Lodge No. 377 for financial irregularities and
disharmony; Van Nuys Lodge No. 450 for a lack of qualified officers, administrative and financial deficiencies, meeting without a quorum, and mismanagement of the hall association; the Maya Lodge No. 793 suspension was continued from the previous year for selling their hall without Masonic Properties
approval; Rosemead Lodge No. 457 for violations of our provisions on alcohol;
Exeter Lodge No. 303 and Olive Branch Lodge No. 269 for significant building improvements without proper approvals; and Delano-Wasco Lodge No.
309 for completing a real estate transaction without the approval of Masonic
Properties. I was happy to reinstate the Charters of Olive Branch Lodge No. 269,

48

Proceedings of the

Exeter Lodge No. 303, Rosemead Lodge No. 457, and Maya Lodge No. 793 after
they met all the requirements under suspension.
Here are some other stats you may wish to know: we attended one 100year lodge anniversary, two 125-year lodge anniversaries and four 150-year
lodge anniversaries. We completed two cornerstone ceremonies, including
the new Health Center in Covina attended by nearly 1,000 people.
Branding and public relations has been a passion of mine. I was hoping
to be much further along than we are in promoting our Square and Compass
and what it stands for, but the priority just did not reach the level I expected.
I am pleased that at least 24 lodges participated in our Open House Month in
September. The lodges that participated were happy with the results—some
of which had hundreds in attendance and dozens of new prospects were identified. We will evaluate the impact of the Open House program and hopefully
more lodges will participate in the future.
Our Masters and Wardens Retreats along with the Secretary and Treasurers
and Inspectors Retreats have been extremely well attended. The agendas and
content are constantly reviewed, so it is erroneous to believe that once you
have been to one, you don’t need to attend one again. These retreats should be
included in your lodge budget and your officers—including the Senior Deacon—
should attend for the future success of your lodge and district. If we are to have
a positive effect on society, we need serious planning and commitment.
It’s stated every year by each Grand Master that the Grand Lodge staff does
a great job. Now I know as only a Grand Master can the depth of involvement
of the staff in making each year successful. Those on the Grand Lodge staff are
not simply great, they are outstanding and amazing. Our Grand Secretary is so
unique and so versatile in his skills, he makes us all look like heroes. My sincere
thanks for everything you and your staff have done for Julie and I since I was
selected Junior Grand Warden recommendee. We are so grateful.
We also thank our Grand Family for being the great Grand Lodge Officers
and spouses we knew you would be.
Lastly, but of course not least in any way, I would like to publicly acknowledge and praise my wife Julie for her patience, devotion, class, and support—
for which I am so indebted. She is my rock and I love her dearly.
Thank you, Brethren, for this very memorable and rewarding journey. I beat
the drum in Sacramento, jumped the poles in Oxnard, sang to Julie in Beverly
Hills, and danced the Hula in Bellflower—many unexpected talents were revealed.
It was far above my expectations and I am so proud to have represented you.
Thank you so much for the difference you made in me.
Respectfully submitted,

Stuart A. Wright, Grand Master

63

REPORT OF THE
DEPUTY GRAND MASTER
2019–2020 GRAND LODGE BUDGET
John E. Trauner, Deputy Grand Master

Brethren of the Grand Lodge of California,
At the last Annual Communication, the brethren representing our
lodges adopted the per capita proposal I presented as Senior Grand Warden.
I am grateful for the support and it has allowed me to present the following
budget for the 2019-2020 grand lodge year.
Revenue for the year is expected to be slightly higher than the current
year, although income from per capita is relatively flat. Expenses align with the
revenue and the budget is balanced with a small surplus.
This budget will allow us to continue the programs and services that our
members and lodges rely upon and which aid us in providing a rewarding
membership experience, meaningful and memorable degrees, strong lodges
and halls, and a positive impact on society. Programs and services supported
by this budget include:
• Financial services to lodges and halls including accounting services,

tax return services, and tax-exempt status restoration

• New lodge development efforts that have already resulted in the

creation of more than 20 new lodges throughout the state

• Leadership training events including the Masters and Wardens

Retreats, Secretary and Treasurer Retreats, Inspector Retreats,
the Inspector Development Academy, and the Lodge Management
Certification Program

• Masonic education including support for events like the

International Conference on Freemasonry at UCLA, the Annual
Symposium, and the Candidate Learning Center

64

Proceedings of the
• Technology and data including iMember, the Member Center, and

the Vault

• Ritual education and training including ritual conferences for

Inspectors, officers’ coaches and lodge officers, and the annual
Ritual Competition

• Communications to Masons, widows, and the general public includ-

ing the lodge app; new lodge website templates; the bimonthly
publication of the California Freemason magazine; the monthly
electronic newsletter The Leader sent to all lodge officers; all-member emails; as well as the maintenance of over 100 lodge and grand
lodge websites and all of the social media outlets

• Community outreach that includes grand lodge events at commu-

nity libraries, courthouses, fire stations, and schools throughout the
state

• Information and service requests
• Property and liability insurance services
• Real estate services including support and consultation for building

improvements, leases, sales, and purchases

Expenses exclusive of depreciation for the next fiscal year are estimated
to be $3,358,359. These expenses are divided between Fraternal, appropriations, programs, and general and administrative expenses. The projected
net revenue after expenses is $18,122. The Executive Committee and Finance
Committee closely monitor the budget and we seek the assistance of the
Executive Committee, Grand Treasurer, Grand Secretary, and the Finance
Committee to see that we operate according to it.
As Deputy Grand Master, I am excited about the future of our Fraternity.
In 2020, we will start the third decade of the 21st century. This represents a
golden opportunity to make a profound difference with our Craft and in the
communities we support.
I appreciate your past support on the per capita proposal I made as
Senior Grand Warden, and I thank you for your support now as we position
Freemasonry as a relevant and respected fraternity for the next decade and
beyond!
Sincerely and fraternally,
John E. Trauner, Deputy Grand Master

Grand Lodge F. & A . M. of California

73

INSTALLATION ADDRESS
John E. Trauner, Grand Master
I am—proud to be—a Mason
Most Worshipful Past Grand Masters, most distinguished visitors, Grand Officers,
Brethren, ladies and friends:
I am—proud to be—a Mason
Those seven words are exceedingly important in my life. I say them every
day and live my life to exemplify them to my very best. I truly believe in what
they stand for and the ideals they embody.
Today I stand before you simply as a Master Mason from a small town,
with a funny name. To say I am humbled simply is not enough. Your faith and
support gratifies me to my very core. Today is truly a most wonderful day in
my life.
I want to thank Most Worshipful Bill Bray for nominating me, and Most
Worshipful’s Bruce Galloway, David Perry and Russ Charvonia for being a part
of my installation. Each of you have been wonderful mentors and are true
friends, always showing me the right path. At this time, I also want to thank my
family, especially my beautiful wife Dana Lynn, who has always supported me
throughout my Masonic career. Simply said, without her I would not be here
today. And lastly, I need to thank my late father, Worshipful John T. Trauner,
who laid down his working tools in 2004 and who inspires me every day. My
dad, my single greatest hero, a man who raised me in life and raised me in my
Third Degree, coached me and mentored me in my Masonic journey. I wear his
past master’s ring every day to keep him close to me.
As most of you know, I hail from the heart of the Gold Country, and I
intend to highlight that historic part of California during my term. However,
all California lodges are special and share a unique piece of California history.
The Gold Country, a swath of land 300 miles long and 50 miles wide in
the mountains and foothills of the Sierra Nevada where the vast majority of
California gold was discovered, was the origin of our Grand Lodge. To set the
stage and to start our journey back to our California Masonic roots, a short
video of the history of our Grand Lodge and a little of my family was made.

74

Proceedings of the

Please watch the screens now.
[video shown]
Thank you for your applause of this wonderful video. I cannot thank
enough the members of MLI, or Masonic Life Initiative of Division VIII, led by
Worshipful Frank Lee, Jack Rose, Walter McCurry, John Channon, and many
other dedicated Masons. Please join me in my heartfelt appreciation for their
hundreds of hours of hard work to create this video.
[applause]
When I was first recommended for the progressive line, I sought the
advice of many of my friends and mentors who are Past Grand Masters. Their
collective advice was mostly similar, and each said in their own way, “Always
be yourself and do not try to emulate or become a person you’re not.”
[Cowboy Hat]
So with that common advice, here I am, simply a country Mason being me,
straightforward and true to my heritage.
As we journey during this next Masonic year, let us remember to be the
Masons that Make a Difference. Those golden opportunities, both large and
small, are the synergistic abilities that define us. Take advantage of all opportunities in front of you. All of us are charged with preserving our past and
inspiring our future. With great pride we honor our past, and with the same
pride we look forward, shaping our future, for it is that very future where the
very best days of Freemasonry lives. As Masons we stand upon the shoulders
of those great men who toiled before us, defining our ideals and values—300
hundred years of history being our greatest inheritance of all. We are all
tied together by our Masonic memories, traditions, and experiences. These
ideals we embrace as we Rise and Build upon each legacy and success, never
doubting that if we truly improve ourselves, we can and must help to Repair
the World.
Sometimes it is a good thing to repeat the past. These ideals and thoughts
come from our most recent Past Grand Masters and ring as true today as when
they were first were spoken. Let us always remember each of those words as
we march forward, together, for an even brighter Masonic future.
My Brothers, our roots run deep throughout the California Gold Country,
where men first came in 1848 to find their fortunes. As you saw in our video,
these men, many of whom were Masons, discovered that others working
next to them were Masons as well from states like Missouri, Iowa, Nebraska,
Wisconsin, and even farther away. Eventually this set the stage to create small
rudimentary mining camp lodges along rivers and streams, which eventually

Grand Lodge F. & A . M. of California

75

grew into larger lodges. As the video showed, many of these Mason miners
eventually ventured into our great Central Valley and were instrumental in
establishing our first five lodges that came together in April 1850 at the Red
House in Sacramento to establish our California Grand Lodge and elect our
first Grand Master, John Stevenson. It is these pioneering forefathers that built
the first framework of our constitution and created the California Masonic
foundation we now stand upon. So that was our past, our very roots, but let
us now look forward. Brethren, we should not be driven by the future—rather,
let us define it.
Yes, Freemasonry has come many miles, and we have many miles yet to
travel. Some of these miles may be over a rough and rugged road, but our
ideals, values, and rich history will always carry us forward. Because being
a Mason means we are value-based and are inclusive and civil toward all
people, no matter their station in life, their origin, religious or professional
background, sexual orientation, or ethnicity. It is the quality of men that
define us because Freemasonry has, and always will, value character over
pedigree, integrity over economic standing, and the ability to be genuine in
ethics and values.
We see golden opportunities all around us. Yes, any opportunity is work,
but it is work that repays itself many times over the effort needed to accomplish the task. Be the Mason who is an agent for change and action, one who
seeks out all challenges and opportunity, and one who is the first to raise a
hand to volunteer.
Embrace those opportunities to help our Youth Orders thrive; to be more
than just a name on a roster for our concordant and appendant bodies; to
continue our philanthropic endeavors in both our foundation and our crown
jewel of Masonry: our Masonic Homes. Remember my Brothers, we will not
be judged by how much we have, but rather by how much we give. Our current
“Let’s Write the Future” campaign has once again proven that we all embrace
this simple statement.
Brethren, just as all Grand Masters who have come before me, we too will
be busy during our year together. As mentioned, we intend to highlight those
pioneering lodges in the Gold Country of California, many of which were
located in or near the Golden Chain Highway 49 in the Motherlode. Our new
coffee table book takes a refreshed look at these small yet defining lodges in
our California Masonic history. I intend to establish a Sister Lodge Program
wherein larger urban and smaller rural lodges will connect and celebrate each
other and learn from each other through activities and events.
In this upcoming year, we will celebrate the centennial anniversary
of Grand Master Charles Adams, who in 1920, established our first Public
School Week, which later became the Public Schools Month that we celebrate
today. One hundred years ago, Grand Master Adams asked California lodges
and Masons to bolster a decaying public schools system in our state during
extremely hard economic times. I ask the same of you now. Let’s make the

76

Proceedings of the

100th anniversary of Public Schools Month in April 2020 a milestone in our
support of public education.
In addition, we will celebrate Mother Mick and the centennial anniversary of Job’s Daughters International, which she founded in 1920 in Omaha,
Nebraska to build character and teach leadership and values to young girls.
I will encourage our lodges to support our Restoration Program. We need
to welcome those Brothers who simply could not pay their annual dues for a
variety of personal reasons, back into our lodges where they can once again
make a valuable difference. I encourage every lodge to join our Restoration
Program, which will restore those suspended brothers, chosen by the lodge,
with a restoration payment of $100. Many of these men need help in finding
their way back into our lodges, so let us help them find their way.
I intend to continue the Special Committee on Leadership Development,
creating training syllabi for all levels of leadership throughout our great
Fraternity. Because, simply stated, the strongest lodges, boards, and committees have the strongest leaders guiding them.
During our year, we intend to continue to build upon the foundation of
our 2050 vision to make sure our great Fraternity is relevant and ready for our
bicentennial. At the same time and with your help, we will start to build our
next operational plan, or 2025 Fraternity plan to take us on the right path, at
the right time, and in the right way.
I strongly believe that just as many of us have renewed our wedding vows,
so should we as Masons renew our obligations. We each should stop and take
a moment to reflect upon why we are, and continue to be, Masonic Brothers. I
will encourage lodge Masters at least once during their term to call for a complete Roll Call of every Brother in their lodge, not simply by sending an email
or leaving a phone message, but by personally inviting them back to their
lodge rooms to participate with their Brothers in our Ceremony of Obligation
Renewal. I believe that if we can remind ourselves why we are Brothers, then
perhaps, some of the disagreements we have had in the past will be replaced
by genuine Brotherly Love and Affection.
Also, during our term together, there will be a World Conference in Israel
in late May 2020, to which I know many of you will want to travel with Dana
and I to celebrate international fraternal relations from around the world. I
intend to have a Grand Masters World Conference tour, about which information will be forthcoming.
I also intend to rename and refresh our current Grand Master Mason of
the Year Award, to reflect truly what it is. It will become the Grand Master’s
Lifetime Achievement Award, recognizing a Mason for his life-long devotion
to the Craft. At the same time, I will create a new award: The Annual Grand
Master’s Mason of the Year Award. Two such awards will be presented annually, one from the north and one from the south. I do not intend for this award
to detract or diminish in any way the wonderful current events by many blue
lodges and Masonic organizations for their own Mason of the Year programs.

Grand Lodge F. & A . M. of California

77

Those are regional or local; this will be a statewide award. I believe we simply
cannot honor our brothers in too many ways!
And lastly, in keeping with Grand Master Wright’s recommendation to me
to study the positioning of our Masonic Center for Youth and Families program (MCYF), I am asking that the Masonic Homes, in coordination with the
Executive Committee, initiate a comprehensive study into the best business
model to support an expansion of this vital program and to look at what structural changes would be needed to attract added funding sources to achieve
this desired outcome. I will monitor the progress of this study and will share
its recommendations with you during our year, when possible, and at our next
Annual Communication.
And finally, my Brethren, I believe in each of you, in what you do and
the Masonic ideals you embody. Each of you are charged with preserving our
roots and providing inspirational leadership to our future. Let this charge
light your pathway toward a Masonic year filled with success and genuine
Brotherly Love.
Remember Brethren, the only real journey is the one within your own heart.
As you travel on your Masonic pathway, remember to keep your heart
above your head. Let it be your guiding light as you travel this wonderful journey, for it will never let you down, and your heart will never lie to you.
Brethren, I am only one Master Mason. I ask that you join with me and
help me as we walk together, on the level, shoulder to shoulder, building upon
the legacies and successes of those great men who have traveled before us, in
a continued and unerring search for our Perfect Ashlars. Together, we can and
we will, accomplish all things.
I am—proud to be—a Mason!
Thank you and God bless each of you and our great California Fraternity!
I love you all.

Grand Lodge F. & A . M. of California

REPORT OF THE
SENIOR GRAND WARDEN
PER CAPITA RECOMMENDATION FOR 2020/2021
Arthur H. Weiss, Senior Grand Warden

Brethren of the Grand Lodge of California,
I am pleased to present this proposal for the per capita assessment that will
be collected in 2020 to fund the fiscal year operations of Grand Lodge for the
period of November 1, 2020 through October 31, 2021.
Over the last two years, I have worked with various committees and
Grand Lodge Officers to create this proposal. Our goal has been to position
the Fraternity for success over the next three decades. The proposal fosters
our current programming while enhancing services to our lodges and members. Earlier this year, I shared these plans with the Masters and Wardens who
attended our spring leadership retreats. I appreciate your input.
In preparing a draft budget for FY 2020/2021, I have considered the factors that will increase per capita, as well as those that will reduce any increase.
The major factors that will increase the per capita are:
• Membership decline. We project a total loss of 1,241 billable mem-

bers. This represents a loss in revenue of $63,133 or $1.57 in per
capita.

• Expenses. Total expenses are only 2.4% over the previous year,

which includes $41,000 to fund the entire cost of Intacct for
lodges. Lodges currently pay an annual fee in addition to per capita
for Intacct use. With this proposal, that additional fee will be eliminated beginning November 2020. The total impact on increased
expenses represents an increase in per capita of $1.71.

These factors together would require an increase in per capita of $3.28.
However, a number of factors will reduce per capita, including a $25,000
increase in dividends from the Nob Hill Masonic Center and increases in

82

Proceedings of the

revenue from investments and all other sources by $16,606. With these factors, the necessary per capita increase can be lowered by $1.03 to $2.25.
Therefore, the per capita I am proposing for FY 2020/2021 is $53.00.
At this per capita rate, we are projecting the total amount of per capita
collected will be $2,132,3439, which is only 1.3% more than in the previous year.
As we embrace the next evolution of our Fraternity, we remain focused on
the four pillars of our current strategic plan: a rewarding member experience,
meaningful and memorable degrees, strong lodges and halls, and our impact
on society. I look forward to working with you and all of our leadership in
preparing the next plan to shape the future of Freemasonry in California. This
proposal will aid in that effort. Thank you for your support!
Sincerely and fraternally,
Arthur H. Weiss, Senior Grand Warden

REPORT OF THE
GRAND TREASURER
Most Worshipful Grand Master and Brethren All:
In this my fourth address to you as your Grand Treasurer, I am pleased to
report to you that the financial health of our Grand Lodge and Related Entities
remains strong. We continue to benefit from the efforts and expertise of many
Brothers who volunteer their time as board members and committee members, as well as the expertise of our entire Grand Lodge financial team led
by: Tom Boyer, our CFO; Maribel Pasamic, our Controller; Khalil Sweidy, our
Director of Financial Planning; and of course, Very Worshipful Allan Casalou,
our Grand Secretary.
The Audit Committee, led by Worshipful Tony Garcia, has chosen to continue our engagement with Moss Adams as our outside auditor to ensure that
our financial statement audits for all of our Grand Lodge entities continues
to go smoothly. As of our last fiscal year ending October 31, 2018, each of our
entities once again received a clean audit opinion and were informed that our
internal controls remain effective and that our model for shared service costs
is not only appropriate but consistent with industry standards.
The Finance Committee, led by Worshipful Levon Keshishian, was
restructured this last year, bringing fresh eyes and a broader corporate experience to our budgeting process in working with our Deputy Grand Master and
Senior Grand Warden to provide wise and timely counsel in the preparation of
their annual budgets and per capita determinations.
The Insurance Committee, led by Worshipful David Forsyth, continues
their tireless work in their detailed review of our complex insurance needs
for not only our Grand Lodge entities but also for our lodges and hall associations. This work includes an ongoing review of claims to ensure an optimal
result for the benefit of the Craft and to look for ways to do all of this in the
most cost-efficient manner.
The Investments Committee, led by Worshipful Eric Hatfield, is deeply
immersed in their ongoing efforts to monitor the economic factors that
impact our portfolio. In their ongoing evaluation of our investment policies,
they continue to recommend that 4.5% of our investment portfolio be distributed to fund the Grand Lodge operating budget which will also work to

90

Proceedings of the

preserve and grow our overall portfolio for future use. The relationship with
NEPC as our investment advisory firm, which began two years ago, continues to provide a great perspective on our various fund managers and allows
the committee to have meaningful discussions with those managers and
provide a deeper dive on our asset allocations. I would also like to mention
that Worshipful Eric Hatfield, who has served as chair for the last four years
and a member of the committee since 2010, has now termed out and I wish
to thank him for his passion, dedication, and expertise that he so willingly
brought to this committee.

the nine-month period through July 31, 2019 compared against the audited
